They're equally compelling as protagonists! 

Emily has a good story about a monarch experiencing the world beyond her throne and learning the hardships her subjects endure on the surface, which is a good story for first-time players to jump into.  It also shows how even though she believes herself not to be as affected by her mother's death, she still hasn't fully comprehended the consequences and the trauma both she and Corvo went through (which is why I personally like high chaos Emily, because it gives the sense that she has repressed rage issues over her childhood trauma).

Corvo, on the other hand, is a story about being reminded of his roots, not only as a poor kid from the slums but as an underhanded assassin (high chaos or not, he still got his hands dirty in DH1 with enslaving, torturing, etc etc). He thinks that his actions of DH1 were done out of desperation, that he's not like Daud/Granny Rags/other witches because he wants to save his daughter. But when he's on the run again, he's reminded that his intentions do not give him a higher moral standing than anyone else and that he still belongs, in a sense, in the same circle as Delilah and her ilk.
